Sorry if I sound preachy, but perhaps we need to have a honest discussion about why health costs are so high. Is it insurers?

A quick explanation in no particular order -

  1. Private insurers. They always try to negotiate or lowball prices, and there's no consistency to it, so medical professionals put up an exorbitant price, knowing the price will go down.

  2. Length and cost of education. Going to medical school is very fucking difficult. It takes years, and years to get through it, and it costs a shit ton of money. The cost of education includes both time and money, because when you're studying you're not bringing in money, which means you're losing out financially. So, you can't just look at the cost of medical school alone. You have to look at the time investment.

  3. Not everyone pays. Sometimes people don't pay, so others are charged to make up for that fact. Of course this sort of exacerbates the problem.

  4. High demand. Healthcare isn't really optional, so there's a certain aspect to it where the professionals treating you can charge the price they believe is fair, rather than what the consumer wants.

  5. Liabilities! People get sued all the time, with or without liability insurance. This makes practicing healthcare very expensive. It's not like another business, where everything is relatively safe, and you have confidence you won't get sued. Since medicine and health is so complicated you cannot be certain your patient's health will improve, and some people will sue because of that.

  6. Medical supplies are very expensive. You need medicine? You need x-ray equipment, and all that stuff? It costs a fuckton of money. We're talking anywhere from thousands of dollars to a million dollars. Everything in the healthcare industry costs a lot of money because of the liabilities involved, and the research, and development.

  7. Real estate. This is a minor one that many people don't consider, but a lot of medical professionals have to rent their own place, which means they have real estate costs to deal with. When you're in a big city like New York, or LA, or whatever, that costs you money.

  8. Multiple employees. You don't have just one person doing you up. When you go to the dentist's office they have the dental assistant, and the secretary. That's three people you're paying for. It's not like dropping into the barber shop, where you only have to deal with one person, mostly.

People will ask, "How come it's so much cheaper in other countries?" They're different countries. They don't require the same oversight or stringent standards as the USA. If that Mexican doctor kills you, guess how much your family's getting in compensation? Nothing.

Of course there is the possibility of reducing prices. I'm not saying that's impossible. But there are a lot of reasons why things cost what they cost.
